messages:
ben: Heads-up — noticed a regression in prefix cache hit-rate on the canary pool after the kernel selection change and the batching heuristic tweak rolled ~2h ago. Warmup cohorts show ~8% lower cold-hit for short prefixes. Anyone else seeing this?
rachel: :eyes: saw a spike in missed prefixes on cohort A, correlates with requests that include tool/fn fields in different orders. Might be keying.
omar: Deploy summary from ci-bot?
ci-bot: test/deploy v3.14.2 -> canary (kernel-bump+batching-heuristic). All integration tests passed.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout at 11:12 UTC. 12/12 hosts healthy.
ben: here's a quick readout from the p50 hit-rate probe across cohorts (short prefixes <32 tokens):
```
cohort A (tool-heavy): before 0.72 -> after 0.64
cohort B (chat-like): before 0.81 -> after 0.78
cohort C (system-prompt pinned): before 0.88 -> after 0.87
```
rachel: that drop on A is worrying. Tool arguments ordering can change cachekey unless we canonicalize. Are we doing stable serialization for tool/function call fields?
omar: We canonicalize tool args in most places but the new kernel path serializes tokenmeta differently (we left a fast path that preserves insertion order). Looks like the kernel-specific serializer missed the canonicalizer.
nora: Is tokenizer version pinning involved? IIRC a tokenizer micro-version bump happened with the kernel patch (tokenizer v2.1.3 -> v2.1.4) and we didn't pin probe agents. A small tokenization diff can change signatures.
ben: Good catch. Probe agents show identical token counts for most, but there are cases where whitespace splits changed. That would flip prefix keys.
rachel: Two actionable items: 1) force canonical tool args (sort keys, normalize JSON) in the kernel fast path; 2) pin tokenizer version inside prefetch/warmup agents so cache-warmup payloads match production.
omar: Agreed. Quick patch I sketched:
```
// kernel fast serializer
// normalize tool args to canonical json with sorted keys, no trailing spaces
string canonicalize_toolargs(map args) {
  return json_dumps(args, sort_keys=true, ensure_ascii=false);
}
```
ben: Also we should consider including a system-prompt hash segment in the cache key unless clients explicitly opt-out. Some of these misses were because system prompt changes are not being included and warmup jobs used older system prompts.
nora: That will increase key cardinality. Maybe make it optional via route config: include_system_prompt = true|false. Warmup jobs can set true.
rachel: For immediate mitigation, can we roll back the kernel fast path to fallback path that already canonicalizes?
omar: Yes, we can flip a runtime flag to force fallback while we patch. Perf cost is ~3% latency p95 for the fallback but saves hit-rate.
ben: Do it. Rollback flag then a small patch to serializer + tokenizer pin for warmup agents. Who takes the rollback?
omar: I'll flip the flag now and watch canary.
ci-bot: feature-flag rollback_cachefast -> enabled at 11:46 UTC by omar.
ben: After rollback, re-run warmup cohort A and report hit-rate in ~5m.
ci-bot: warmup job kickoff: warmup/prefix-cohort-A v2 at 11:49 UTC.
rachel: Also add a short-term metric: tool-arg-order-hit-ratio tag to see how many misses correlate with non-canonical field order.
ben: Good idea — low effort metric. Nora can you add to console dashboard?
nora: Yep, putting a panel under 'prefix-cache -> keying' with a filter for has_tool_args=true.
ben: Postmortem note: kernel-level serializer must call shared canonicalization util or we risk divergent keying across runtime paths. Add to checklist.
omar: Patch PR incoming: kernel-serializer -> call PrefetchKey.canonicalize(). Also pin warmup agents tokenizer to v2.1.3 in their job spec. I'll link PR shortly.
ben: Thanks. If fallback fixes hit-rate we can release the serializer patch in a follow-up canary.
omar: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/patches/2345
both: :thumbsup:
